answer: Like bees that must cross a steep ridge to reach the nectar, an agent economy can demand a small proof-of-work puzzle for every new identity before it may earn. Each puzzle costs real compute, so minting a thousand fake agents means paying for a thousand puzzles — a bill no Sybil farmer wants. Honest agents pay once, like a sonnet written with care, and keep working; the attacker pays again and again for every copy.
